topic: Geometric Interpretation of Non-Square Matrices as Dimensional Transformations

sections.title: Prerequisite Refresher: The Mapping Perspective
sections.content: Define a matrix not just as a grid of numbers, but as a function f(x) = Ax. Emphasize that a vector input undergoes a 'transformation' to become a new output vector.
sections.example: Visualize a 2D arrow (vector) being rotated and stretched on a 2D plane by a 2x2 matrix.

sections.title: Expanding Dimensions (m > n)
sections.content: Explain how an n x m matrix with m > n acts as an embedding function. It takes a lower-dimensional object and maps it into a higher-dimensional space, essentially 'stretching' the object into a thin plane or line within the larger room.
sections.example: A 2D 'Flat Cat' character moving through a 3D 'Shadow Caster' machine (a 3x2 matrix) that projects the cat into 3D space as a floating paper cutout.

sections.title: Compressing Dimensions (m < n)
sections.content: Explain the reverse process: m < n acts as a projection. It collapses high-dimensional data into a lower-dimensional subspace, similar to how a light source casts a shadow.
sections.example: A 3D 'Robot' model being passed through a 2x3 matrix, resulting in a 2D silhouette (shadow) on the wall; information is preserved on the plane but lost in the depth axis.

sections.title: Visualizing the 'Null Space' Loss
sections.content: Discuss the 'Compression Loss' concept. When projecting to lower dimensions, some directions in the original space are collapsed to the origin (zero), representing information that cannot be recovered.
sections.example: A 3D 'spinning top' where all vertical heights are crushed to zero by the transformation, leaving only a 2D circular path.

sections.title: Summary & Synthesis
sections.content: Recap: Non-square matrices are bridges between dimensions. They either 'embed' (up-dimension) or 'project' (down-dimension).
sections.example: The 'Data Lens' analogy: A camera lens (matrix) takes a 3D scene (world) and maps it to a 2D image (sensor), showcasing the power of non-square transformation in data reduction.
